incident-bot: ALERT: p99 request latency > 5s for /v1/chat/streaming (hosts: us-west-2, eu-west-1) — paging: tokenizer/preproc queue growth. Auto-paged to #incidents.

Sara: Paging oncall — saw multiple >5s p99 spikes starting ~1797654000. Streaming stalls reported by two customers.

Matt: digging into traces now, looks like preproc stage (tokenizer + prompt builder) is the dominant tail. p95 ~ 600ms, p99 ~ 5.6s.

Rui: I see lots of re-tokenizations on the same prompt template. Many requests hitting JSON-mode tool schema expand path. Could be template + tool schema growth on the hot route.

Sara: Customer message from acct-team: "Users experience long stalls while streaming responses — partial tokens then gap." They saw retries. Flagging potential SLO breach.

pgilmore: Confirmed: dashboard shows sharp increase in preproc queue length at 1797654012, correlates with spike in streaming tail latency.

aliceops: Any recent deploys or prompt changes?

Matt: No deployment around that time. But config push to templates service at 1797653950 added a new tool schema with large JSON examples for the payments tool.

Rui: That matches: large tool schema + JSON mode triggers deep prompt construction (serialize examples + validate + pretty-print) before tokenization. The serialization step calls into python jsonschema -> heavy CPU.

Sara: Logs snippet: ```
preproc: start request id=abc123 route=/chat/streaming
preproc: build_prompt template=payments_with_schema v=2.4.1
preproc: schema_expand duration=4230ms
preproc: tokenize duration=120ms
preproc: total=4353ms
```

Matt: So schema_expand is the hotspot (~4s). Tokenize smaller. That explains streaming stalls (no tokens flushed while preproc runs).

incident-bot: INCIDENT: SLO at risk (streaming tail). Notifying SRE and Product oncall.

Sara: Mitigation options — list what we can do live: 1) Rollback template change in templates service. 2) Short-circuit JSON-mode expansion for streaming route. 3) Route affected customers to smaller model variant or to non-streaming endpoint with pre-warmed caches. 4) Add emergency prefix cache TTL on the template. 5) Increase dedicated preproc worker count.

pgilmore: Quick check: how risky is rollback? The template push changed example block only. Rolling back is straightforward but has to pass config validation.

aliceops: We can flip a feature flag to disable schema expansion — low-risk, immediate. Need approval from Sara/product.

Sara: Do it. Flip ff:templates:expand_json_examples=false for streaming route. Notify me when done.

Matt: Applying flag now -> ```curl -X POST https://templates.internal/flags -d '{"key":"templates.expand_json_examples","value":false,"scope":"route:chat/streaming"}'``` -> 200.

Rui: Observability: preproc queue length is dropping already. p99 down from 5.6s -> 1.1s within two minutes.

incident-bot: UPDATE: SLO alert cleared for p99. Continue monitoring for regressions.

Sara: Customer-facing status: please prepare short note: "We observed streaming stalls caused by prompt pre-processing of expanded JSON tool examples. We disabled the example expansion for streaming to restore latency while we fix the templates."

pgilmore: Oncall handoff: I'm taking incident lead for next 2 hours to stabilize and own root cause. Handoff to matt at 1797655200.

aliceops: Action items: [1] Rework templates to remove large example blobs (owner: product, due: 1797730000). [2] Add unit-time budget in preproc for JSON-mode (owner: eng-runtime, due: 1797690000). [3] Add i18n to prefix cache to reduce re-serializations (owner: eng-ml, due: 1797710000).

Matt: Follow-up: we'll add runtime guard for streaming route that bypasses heavy schema validation; prefer lightweight schema fingerprinting + async validation.

Rui: Also adding a telemetry tag to identify requests that use JSON-mode heavy schema so we can throttle or route them differently next time.

Sara: Thanks team. Any customer still reporting issues ping me. I'll draft status page update.

pgilmore: Closing loop: rollback not needed, flag did the job. Will keep monitoring until next handoff.

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: streaming tail latency restored to SLO. Root cause: large tool schema examples triggered expensive preproc expansion in JSON-mode. Postmortem planned.

Sara: Postmortem owners assigned to pgilmore + matt + rui. Please schedule postmortem within 48 hours and include mitigation plan + tests to prevent template pushes that exceed preproc budget.

Matt: Noted. Will include reproducer and perf test harness for templates service.

Rui: I'll open follow-up PR to add async serialization path and to emit per-request preproc timings to aid future triage.

aliceops: Adding customer follow-up tasks to support queue.

Sara: Thanks everyone. Updating #customer-impact channel and closing paging. :white_check_mark:
